class.name: ResourceImporterDirectStorageTexture
class.brief_description: Imports an image for use as a DirectStorage compressed texture ([DSTex]).
class.description: This importer imports [DSTex] ([code].dstex[/code]) compressed texture resources for DirectStorage-accelerated streaming. Image files ([code].png[/code], [code].jpg[/code], [code].jpeg[/code], [code].webp[/code]) are processed with optional VRAM block compression (S3TC or BPTC) and compressed using Microsoft GDeflate. During export, [EditorExportPlugin] bundles [code].dstex[/code] resources into [code]res://textures.dspkg[/code] via [DSPkg], allowing [DSResourceFormatLoader] and [DSContext] to stream textures directly to GPU or CPU memory at runtime. Presets: [b]Project Default[/b] follows [code]directstorage/import/default_profile[/code]; [b]3D (Streaming)[/b] is the product default; [b]CPU / ImageTexture (2D, UI, Decals)[/b] keeps 2D and UI assets on the CPU path. A pure 2D project should normally use Godot's [ResourceImporterTexture] instead. See also [ResourceImporterTexture], [DSTex], and [DSContext]. [b]Migration:[/b] the old [code]compression/source[/code] option was replaced by [code]compression/color_space[/code], [code]compress/normal_map[/code], and [code]compress/channel_pack[/code]. Existing [code].import[/code] files that only store the old key are mapped automatically on the next import; once any of the new keys is written, it takes precedence.

members.member: The Microsoft GDeflate compression level applied to the texture data payload in the generated [code].dstex[/code] file, ranging from [code]1[/code] through [code]12[/code]. Lower values (such as the default [code]1[/code]) maximize encoding speed in the editor and provide the highest DirectStorage decompression throughput. Higher values achieve smaller file sizes on disk at the cost of slower import times and increased decompression workload.

Selects the color space stored in the [code].dstex[/code] header: [b]Linear:[/b] Linear data such as normal maps, roughness, metallic, masks, or lookup tables. The loader creates a linear (UNORM) GPU format. [b]sRGB:[/b] Standard color texture (such as albedo or diffuse maps). The loader creates the sRGB counterpart of the GPU format so hardware sampling decodes it to linear correctly. This option is independent from channel packing: it only records how the stored values must be interpreted.

Controls normal-map processing: [b]Disabled:[/b] Treat the image as ordinary color/data. [b]Enabled:[/b] Normalize the base level and renormalize mip levels, and prioritize the red/green channels during block compression. With [code]compression/high_quality[/code] the result is BC7; disable it to get BC5/BC3 normal-map formats. Usage-based auto-detection is not available to a custom importer; enable this explicitly for normal maps.

Controls channel packing during block compression. Only applies when [code]compression/mode[/code] is [b]VRAM Compressed[/b]: [b]sRGB Friendly:[/b] Detect used channels as sRGB color, avoiding channel packing that would shift values when the texture is sampled as sRGB. [b]Optimized:[/b] Detect used channels as generic data, allowing the codec to pack them more aggressively (smaller files, but not safe for sRGB-sampled color textures).

When [code]compression/mode[/code] is [b]VRAM Compressed[/b], use BPTC/BC7 instead of S3TC. BPTC preserves alpha and normal-map detail better but takes twice the VRAM of BC1 and encodes on the CPU during import. [b]Note:[/b] With BPTC, [code]compress/normal_map[/code] produces BC7, not BC5. Disable this option if BC5 normal maps are preferred.

The compression mode to use for the imported texture. [b]VRAM Compressed:[/b] Compresses texture mipmaps using S3TC (BC1/BC3/BC4/BC5) or, with [code]compression/high_quality[/code], BPTC (BC7) prior to GDeflate compression. This significantly reduces GPU VRAM consumption and optimizes streaming bandwidth. Recommended for standard 3D textures. [b]VRAM Uncompressed:[/b] Retains uncompressed raw pixel data (such as RGBA8) with mipmaps, compressed only on disk using lossless GDeflate. Preserves perfect pixel fidelity with zero block compression artifacts (ideal for pixel art, crisp UI elements, or lookup tables), but requires significantly more memory at runtime.

If [code]true[/code], generate a full mip chain. Disable for 2D/UI textures that are always sampled at 1:1; a disabled chain writes a single-mip [code].dstex[/code] and saves roughly one third of the payload and memory.

If greater than [code]0[/code], resize the image so its longer edge is at most this many pixels before mip generation and compression. [code]0[/code] applies only the 16384-pixel container cap. Useful for mobile targets (4096/8192) and to avoid oversized staging buffers.

Selects the source for the red output channel: Red, Green, Blue, Alpha, Inverted Red/Green/Blue/Alpha, Unused, Zero, or One. Use this with the green/blue/alpha siblings to pack PBR masks into one texture or to flip the green channel of normal maps exported with the opposite Y convention. Applied before normalization and mip generation via [method DSTex.remap_channels].
Selects the source for the green output channel. See [code]process/channel_remap/red[/code].
Selects the source for the blue output channel. See [code]process/channel_remap/red[/code].
Selects the source for the alpha output channel. See [code]process/channel_remap/red[/code].
If [code]true[/code], put surrounding color into the transparent border of RGBA8 images before compression, reducing bilinear-filter halos. Enabled by the CPU/ImageTexture (2D) preset.
If [code]true[/code], premultiply RGB by alpha before compression. Requires materials configured for premultiplied alpha.

Forces the texture to load into CPU memory as an [ImageTexture] even when GPU streaming prewarm ([method DSPreloader.prewarm_gpu_async]) is active. [b]Note:[/b] Standard runtime loads ([ResourceLoader]) and CPU prewarm ([method DSPreloader.prewarm_async]) already create [ImageTexture] resources automatically. This setting is specifically needed for projects using D3D12 GPU prewarm when an asset requires CPU pixel access—such as [Light3D] projectors ([member Light3D.light_projector]), [Decal] textures, or scripts calling [method Texture2D.get_image]—preventing engine atlas warnings and readback stalls. [b]Note:[/b] Some formats never take the GPU prewarm path regardless of this setting: uncompressed and float data formats (R8, RG8, RGB8, the R16 family, float formats, BC6H) are always prewarmed into [ImageTexture]. Color formats with an sRGB counterpart (BC1, BC2, BC3, BC7, the RGBA8/BGRA8 family) and the linear block formats used by 3D material data (BC4, BC5 - which includes normal maps) do use the GPU path.
